question_text:
A 12-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her mother because she has been waking up multiple times at night to go to the bathroom even though she avoids drinking large amounts of water close to bedtime. She has no significant medical history apart from 3 episodes of lower urinary tract infections treated with nitrofurantoin in the past 2 years. Her family emigrated from Nigeria 10 years ago. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 14.2 g/dL
MCV 92 fL
Reticulocytes 1.5%
Serum
Osmolality 290 mOsmol/kg H2O
Urine
Leukocytes negative
Nitrite negative
Glucose negative
Osmolality 130 mOsmol/kg H2O
Hemoglobin electrophoresis shows:
HbA 56%
HbS 43%
HbF 1%
This patient is at greatest risk for which of the following conditions?"?

                    ### Question
                    A 12-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her mother because she has been waking up multiple times at night to go to the bathroom even though she avoids drinking large amounts of water close to bedtime. She has no significant medical history apart from 3 episodes of lower urinary tract infections treated with nitrofurantoin in the past 2 years. Her family emigrated from Nigeria 10 years ago. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 14.2 g/dL
MCV 92 fL
Reticulocytes 1.5%
Serum
Osmolality 290 mOsmol/kg H2O
Urine
Leukocytes negative
Nitrite negative
Glucose negative
Osmolality 130 mOsmol/kg H2O
Hemoglobin electrophoresis shows:
HbA 56%
HbS 43%
HbF 1%
This patient is at greatest risk for which of the following conditions?"?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Necrosis of the renal papillae
opb. Pigment stones in the biliary tract
opc. Autoinfarction of the spleen
opd. Sickling in the cerebral vessels
ope. Transient arrest of erythropoiesis

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient presents with nocturia and low urine osmolality, suggesting a renal concentrating ability issue, likely due to sickle cell disease, as indicated by the significant HbS level (43%). Sickle cell disease is known to increase the risk of renal complications, including renal papillary necrosis, due to vaso-occlusive crises. Additionally, the patient's Nigerian descent supports a higher prevalence of sickle cell disease in this population. While cerebral sickling is a significant risk, the acute nature of renal complications, particularly renal papillary necrosis, is a critical concern in this context. Therefore, the patient is at greatest risk for renal papillary necrosis, supported by the evidence that sickle cell anemia can lead to this condition.
